source.title: Current Open Questions in Complete Mixability

accepted.question_text: Let n be a positive integer and let M_n(μ) denote the set of distributions on ℝ that are n-completely mixable with center μ. If a distribution F on ℝ or on ℝ^d is n-completely mixable, must its center be unique? Equivalently, for distinct μ, ν ∈ ℝ, is M_n(μ) ∩ M_n(ν) empty?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 1. Is the center of mixability always unique for a distribution on R (or R^d)? In other words, for μ, ν ∈ R, μ ≠ ν, is it true that M_n(μ) ∩ M_n(ν) = ∅?

accepted.question_text: Can one develop generic probabilistic or analytic proofs for the main complete-mixability and joint-mixability theorems, rather than relying on long arguments based on combinatorics, discretization of distributions, and mathematical induction?

evidence.quote: However, the proofs of the recent results on complete mixability, namely (b)-(d), are all based on combinatorics and discretization of distributions.
Open Problem 2. Is there a generic (probabilistic, analytic) proof of the main results in complete and joint mixability?

accepted.question_text: Theorem 3 states that a ℤ_+-valued random vector X is a joint mix with joint center N if and only if it can be written as X = ∑_{k=1}^N X_k, where each X_k is a binary multinomial random vector. Can this decomposition be used in a nontrivial way to characterize additional classes of completely mixable or jointly mixable distributions, and if so how?

evidence.quote: Theorem 3. Suppose that X takes values in Z+. X is a joint mix with joint center N ∈ Z+ if and only if it has the following representation X = ∑_{k=1}^N X_k, where X_k, k = 1, . . . , N are binary multinomial random vectors.
Open Problem 3. Is Theorem 3 helpful (and how) in characterizing more classes of CM and JM distributions?

accepted.question_text: Let F be a distribution with mean μ, let X ∼ F, and suppose that for every law-determined norm ∥·∥ and every real t, with s = (nμ - t)/(n - 1), the inequalities ∥(X - t)^+∥ ≤ (n - 1)∥(X - s)^-∥ and ∥(X - t)^-∥ ≤ (n - 1)∥(X - s)^+∥ hold. Under what additional assumptions, possibly including smoothness conditions, are these inequalities sufficient to imply that F is n-completely mixable?

evidence.quote: Theorem 5. Suppose that F is n-CM with center μ, X ∼ F and || · || is any law-determined norm. Then we have that ||(X - t)+|| ≤ (n - 1)||(X - s)−|| and ||(X - t)−|| ≤ (n - 1)||(X - s)+||, (14) for all t ∈ R and s = (nμ - t)/(n - 1).

Open Problem 4. Suppose that F has mean μ, and (14) holds for all law-determined norms || · || and all t ∈ R. (With what extra conditions, possibly some smoothness conditions) is it sufficient for F to be n-CM?

accepted.question_text: If C is a convex subset of ℝ^d, is the uniform distribution on C necessarily n-completely mixable for every n ≥ d + 1?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5. Is a uniform distribution on a convex set C ⊂ R^d necessarily n-CM for all n > d + 1?

accepted.question_text: Let F be a distribution on ℝ^d with d > 1. If the projection of F onto every essential subspace of ℝ^d is n-completely mixable, under what additional conditions does it follow that F itself is n-completely mixable on ℝ^d?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6. Suppose that F is a distribution on R^d, d > 1, and the projection of F to any essential subspace of R^d is n-CM. (With what extra conditions) is it sufficient for F to be n-CM on R^d ?

accepted.question_text: Is every absolutely continuous distribution supported on a bounded interval n-completely mixable once n is large enough?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 7. Are all absolutely continuous distributions on a bounded interval n-CM for large enough n?

accepted.question_text: Suppose a distribution F satisfies a known sufficient condition for n-complete mixability, such as one of the conditions listed earlier in Section 2.2. Can one write down an explicit copula for an n-complete mix with margins F, or more generally for a joint mix with prescribed margins?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 8. Suppose that F satisfies one of the sufficient conditions (for instance, (b) in Section 2.2) and hence is n-CM. What is a possible copula of a n-complete mix with margins F (or a joint mix with given margins)?

accepted.question_text: Suppose a distribution F satisfies a known sufficient condition for n-complete mixability, such as one of the conditions listed earlier in Section 2.2. Is there a way to simulate samples from an n-complete mix with margins F?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 9. Suppose that F satisfies one of the sufficient conditions (for instance, (b) in Section 2.2) and hence is n-CM. Could we simulate sample from a n-complete mix with margins F?

accepted.question_text: For a unimodal distribution supported on a bounded interval, what additional conditions are sufficient to guarantee n-complete mixability?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 10. Under what extra conditions a unimodal distribution on a bounded interval is n-CM?

accepted.question_text: Let D_n be the aggregation set of sums X_1 + ⋯ + X_n formed from random variables with prescribed marginal distributions F_1, …, F_n. What are necessary and sufficient conditions for D_n to contain a smallest element with respect to convex order?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 11. What are necessary and sufficient conditions for Dn to contain a smallest element with respect to convex order?

accepted.question_text: Let D_n be the aggregation set of sums X_1 + ⋯ + X_n formed from random variables with prescribed marginal distributions F_1, …, F_n. How can one characterize D_n, at least for some simple choices of the marginals? Equivalently, given a target distribution G, how can one decide whether there exists S ∼ G with S ∈ D_n?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 12. How can one characterize Dn (maybe for some simple marginal distributions)? That is, for a given distribution G, determine whether S ∈ Dn for some S ∼ G.

accepted.question_text: Given positive numbers a_{i,j} representing the time taken by worker (i, j) to complete production step j, and using permutations σ_1, …, σ_n ∈ S_m to assign one worker from each step to each of m equipments, minimize max_{i=1,…,m} ∑_{j=1}^n a_{σ_j(i),j}. What assignment of workers is optimal, and how can an optimal assignment be computed?

evidence.quote: Here we have two general questions: (i) What is an optimal arrangement (σ_1, . . . , σ_n) for (1)? How could we calculate an optimal arrangement (σ_1, . . . , σ_n)?

accepted.question_text: For the same production-step assignment problem, let T^* = min_{σ_1,…,σ_n∈ S_m} max_{i=1,…,m} ∑_{j=1}^n a_{σ_j(i),j}. Under what conditions does T^* equal the average value (1/m)∑_{i=1}^m∑_{j=1}^n a_{i,j}, and how can T^* be computed?

evidence.quote: (ii) Under what conditions, T^* = 1/m ∑_m_i=1 ∑_n_j=1 a_{i,j}? How could we calculate T^*?

accepted.question_text: For given distributions, can one design effective algorithms to decide whether they are jointly mixable or to solve the minimax assignment problem from Section 1? In particular, under what conditions do the swapping algorithms discussed in the paper converge?

evidence.quote: 1. Algorithms to determine whether some distributions are jointly mixable, or solving question (1) in Section 1: see for instance [28, 12, 34, 19]. The conditions under which the swapping algorithms in [28] converges are still unclear.

accepted.question_text: If one prescribes fixed bivariate or higher-dimensional marginal distributions, when does there exist a joint mix compatible with those marginals, and how can one develop algorithms to determine this numerically?

evidence.quote: 2. Mixability under higher-dimensional constraints: for fixed bivariate or higher-dimensional marginal distributions, determine whether a joint mix exists and develop algorithms for numerical determination.

accepted.question_text: What happens if the definition of mixability uses a multivariate function other than the sum x_1 + ⋯ + x_n? Which alternative multivariate functions lead to useful notions of mixability, and how should those notions be characterized?

evidence.quote: 3. Other multivariate functions replacing the summation of random variables in the definition of mixability; see [4].

accepted.question_text: How does the algebraic structure of the underlying semigroup G affect complete mixability and joint mixability defined on G?

evidence.quote: 4. The influence of the algebraic structure of a semigroup G on complete and joint mixability defined on G.

accepted.question_text: For n > 3, can one fully characterize the set J_n(K) of n-tuples of distributions that are jointly mixable with joint center K, or equivalently the set M_n(μ) of distributions on ℝ that are n-completely mixable with center μ?

evidence.quote: For n = 1 or n = 2, the sets Jn(K) and Mn(μ) are fully characterized. For n > 3, a full characterization of either set is still an open question.
